QuestionText: Euclid's first postulate states:
Options: A) All right angles are equal
B) A straight line may be drawn from any point to any other point
C) A circle can be drawn with any centre and radius
D) The whole is greater than the part
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Euclid's 1st Postulate: A straight line segment can be drawn joining any two points.

QuestionText: Euclid's 5th postulate (parallel postulate) led to:
Options: C) Proof that parallel lines meet
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Euclid's 5th postulate was questioned for centuries, leading to non-Euclidean geometries (Lobachevsky, Riemann) where the 5th postulate doesn't hold.

QuestionText: A point has:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: According to Euclid: A point is that which has no part (no length, breadth, or depth). It is dimensionless.

QuestionText: If two lines intersect, vertically opposite angles are:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Vertically opposite angles (formed by two intersecting lines) are always equal.

QuestionText: Two supplementary angles sum to:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Supplementary angles: sum = 180°. Complementary angles: sum = 90°.

QuestionText: Two complementary angles sum to:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Complementary angles sum to 90°. If one is 30°, its complement is 60°.

QuestionText: When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternate interior angles are:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternate interior angles are equal (Z-angles). This is a key property of parallel lines.

QuestionText: Co-interior angles (same-side interior) formed when parallel lines cut by transversal are:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Co-interior (consecutive interior) angles are supplementary when lines are parallel. Also called C-angles or co-interior angles.

QuestionText: Corresponding angles formed when parallel lines are cut by a transversal are:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Corresponding angles (F-angles) are equal when lines are parallel. They are on the same side of the transversal, one interior, one exterior.

QuestionText: If two lines are perpendicular, the angle between them is:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Perpendicular lines meet at exactly 90°. The symbol ⊥ denotes perpendicularity.

QuestionText: The complement of 35° is:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Complement = 90° − 35° = 55°.

QuestionText: The supplement of 120° is:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Supplement = 180° − 120° = 60°.

QuestionText: If two straight lines intersect, the sum of all four angles formed is:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Four angles formed at intersection: 2 pairs of vertically opposite angles. Together they form a complete rotation = 360°.

QuestionText: An axiom in Euclid's geometry is:
Options: A) A self-evident truth accepted without proof
B) A theorem that needs proof
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Axioms (or common notions) are self-evident truths accepted without proof. Postulates are specific geometric assumptions.

QuestionText: Euclid's 3rd postulate states:
Options: A) A line can be extended indefinitely
B) A circle can be drawn with any centre and radius
C) All right angles are equal
D) Things equal to the same are equal
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: 3rd Postulate: A circle can be described with any centre and radius.

QuestionText: Two lines are parallel if and only if the distance between them is:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Parallel lines are equidistant everywhere. If distance varies, the lines will eventually meet (not parallel).

QuestionText: If ∠1 + ∠2 = 180° and they are on a straight line, then ∠1 and ∠2 are:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Linear pair: two adjacent angles that sum to 180°, formed on a straight line. Linear Pair Axiom: adjacent angles on a line sum to 180°.

QuestionText: Two angles are vertically opposite if they are:
Options: B) Formed by two intersecting lines, opposite to each other
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Vertically opposite angles are formed when two lines intersect, on opposite sides of the intersection point. They are always equal.

QuestionText: Line AB and line CD are parallel. A transversal EF cuts them. If ∠1 = 55° (corresponding to ∠2), then ∠2 = ?
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel. ∠2 = ∠1 = 55°.

QuestionText: If alternate angles formed by transversal are equal, then the lines are:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: If alternate interior angles are equal, the lines are parallel (converse of alternate angle theorem).

QuestionText: The sum of interior angles on the same side of transversal between parallel lines = ?
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Co-interior angles (same-side interior, C-angles) between parallel lines sum to 180°.

QuestionText: An angle that equals its supplement is a:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: If x = 180° − x → 2x = 180° → x = 90°. An angle equal to its own supplement is 90°.

QuestionText: According to Euclid, a theorem:
Options: B) Must be proved using axioms and previously established theorems
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Theorems in Euclidean geometry must be logically proved using axioms, postulates, and previously proven theorems. This is the deductive method.

QuestionText: If two lines AB ∥ CD and a transversal PQ intersects them at E and F respectively. ∠BEF = 70°. ∠EFD = ?
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: ∠BEF and ∠EFD are co-interior angles (same side). Co-interior angles between parallel lines sum to 180°. ∠EFD = 180° - 70° = 110°.

QuestionText: The number of lines that can pass through a single point is:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Infinitely many lines can pass through a single point. But only one line passes through two distinct points.

QuestionText: The angle formed between a line and itself extended (a straight angle) is:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: A straight angle = 180°. It's the angle of a straight line (a half rotation).

QuestionText: If ∠PQR = 70°, ∠QPS = 110°, and PQ is a transversal cutting lines QR and PS, are QR and PS parallel?
Options: B) Yes, co-interior angles sum to 180°
C) No, they are not parallel
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: ∠PQR + ∠QPS = 70° + 110° = 180°. These are co-interior angles summing to 180°, so QR ∥ PS.

QuestionText: A reflex angle is greater than:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Reflex angle: greater than 180° and less than 360°. Acute: 0-90°. Right: 90°. Obtuse: 90-180°. Straight: 180°.

QuestionText: Euclid's axiom 'The whole is greater than the part' means:
Options: A) A subset is always smaller than the set
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: The whole (say AB) is greater than any of its parts (say AC where C is between A and B). AB > AC.

QuestionText: Two angles in a linear pair. One angle is 3x and the other is 2x. Find x.
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Linear pair sums to 180°: 3x + 2x = 180° → 5x = 180° → x = 36°.

QuestionText: Euclid's 2nd postulate states:
Options: A) A circle can be drawn
B) A terminated line (segment) can be extended indefinitely
C) All right angles are equal
D) Things equal to same are equal
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: 2nd Postulate: A terminated line can be extended indefinitely in a straight line.

QuestionText: The angle between two parallel lines is:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Parallel lines never meet and have the same direction, so the angle between them is 0°.

QuestionText: Three or more points are said to be collinear if:
Options: A) They are vertices of a triangle
B) They all lie on the same straight line
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Collinear points lie on the same line. Non-collinear points (minimum 3) determine a unique plane/triangle.

QuestionText: Euclid's 4th postulate states:
Options: A) All right angles are equal to each other
B) A circle can be drawn with any radius
C) A line can be extended
D) The whole is greater than the part
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: 4th Postulate: All right angles are equal to one another. This ensures consistency in right angle measurement everywhere.

QuestionText: If two angles are both equal to a third angle, they are equal to each other. This is based on:
Options: B) Euclid's Axiom (things equal to same thing are equal)
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Euclid's common notion (axiom): 'Things which are equal to the same thing are equal to one another.' If ∠A = ∠C and ∠B = ∠C, then ∠A = ∠B.

QuestionText: An acute angle is between:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Acute angle: strictly between 0° and 90°. Right: exactly 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180°. Reflex: between 180° and 360°.

QuestionText: ∠ABC and ∠DBC share ray BC. ∠ABC + ∠DBC = 180°. Rays BA and BD are:
Options: C) Opposite rays (forming a line AD)
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: If ∠ABC + ∠DBC = 180° and they share ray BC, then rays BA and BD form a straight line (linear pair axiom — opposite rays).

QuestionText: Which of Euclid's common notions states: 'If equals are added to equals, the wholes are equal'?
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: 2nd common notion: If equals are added to equals, the sums are equal. (a = b → a + c = b + c)

QuestionText: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. The alternate exterior angles are:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Alternate exterior angles (both outside the parallel lines, on opposite sides of transversal) are equal — same as alternate interior angles.

QuestionText: If ∠1 and ∠2 are vertically opposite and ∠1 = 4x − 20° and ∠2 = 2x + 40°, find ∠1.
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Vertically opposite are equal: 4x−20=2x+40 → 2x=60 → x=30. ∠1=4(30)−20=120−20=100°.

QuestionText: Three lines meet at one point. The number of angles formed is:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Three lines through one point form 6 angles (3 pairs of vertically opposite angles). Each line creates one pair of vertical angles = 3 pairs = 6 angles.

QuestionText: How many dimensions does a plane have?
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: A plane has 2 dimensions (length and breadth). A line has 1 dimension. A point has 0 dimensions. A solid has 3 dimensions.

QuestionText: Lines l and m are parallel. A transversal n cuts them. The interior angles on one side sum to 200°. Are l and m parallel?
Options: B) No — they must sum to 180° for parallel lines
D) Yes if alternate angles equal
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: For parallel lines, co-interior angles must sum to exactly 180°. If sum = 200° ≠ 180°, the lines are not parallel.

QuestionText: In Euclidean geometry, a line extends:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: A line (in Euclidean geometry) extends infinitely in both directions. A ray has one endpoint and extends infinitely in one direction. A segment has two endpoints.

QuestionText: Adjacent angles share a common vertex and a common side. They:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Adjacent angles share a vertex and one ray but do not overlap. They may sum to 90°, 180°, or any value depending on context.

QuestionText: ∠AOB and ∠BOC are adjacent angles forming ∠AOC = 120°. If ∠AOB = 2∠BOC, find ∠BOC.
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles

QuestionText: Euclid defined a surface as that which has:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Euclid's definition: A surface has length and breadth only (2D). A solid has all three dimensions. A line has only length.

QuestionText: Lines l₁ ∥ l₂. A transversal makes angles of 70° with l₁. The acute angle with l₂ is:
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel. The transversal makes the same angle (70°) with both parallel lines.

QuestionText: If ∠1 = 5x and ∠2 = 4x + 9 are alternate interior angles between two parallel lines, find x.
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal: 5x = 4x + 9 → x = 9.

QuestionText: If two lines are perpendicular and a third line is parallel to one of them, it is __ to the other.
Topic: Mathematics - Euclids Geometry Lines and Angles
Explanation: If l₁ ⊥ l₂ and l₃ ∥ l₁, then l₃ ⊥ l₂. (Two lines both perpendicular to a transversal are parallel to each other; conversely.)
